raw_case_text:
A 54-year-old male patient sought medical attention with a complaint of severe oral pain, ulceration in mouth, facial swelling and difficulty in eating and speaking for the past one month. The patient reported a history of episodes of fever and redness, irritation and swelling in relation to the right eye. In addition, the patient also reported experiencing rashes and pustules over the skin, most commonly on the upper arms for two weeks. The patient was unaware of any significant medical history. Clinical examination revealed extensive ulceration in the right buccal mucosa. The lesion was rapidly progressive, with irregular borders, central necrosis and surrounding erythema [Figure 1]. The skin opposite the lesion did not show any abnormality with no symptoms of paraesthesia. On ocular examination, visual acuity was 20/20 in both eyes; however, redness of conjunctiva was present along with pustules in the lower eyelid of the right eye [Figure 2]. Head-to-toe examination revealed the presence of pruritic rashes in shoulder, trunk, upper arms and lower limbs. Submandibular lymph nodes were normal in size and consistency.
Routine laboratory investigations were advised along with serological tests and the patient was diagnosed as human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) positive. His CD4 cell count was 142 cells/muL which indicated the condition of AIDS. Given the clinical presentation and the patient's immunocompromised status, the differential diagnosis included cancrum oris, SCC, fungal infection, tuberculosis and acute myeloid leukaemia. Ultrasonography was done which revealed lymph nodes normal in size and consistency. A biopsy was carried out with all necessary precautions and wound care and debridement were done. The patient was immediately started on broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics, antiretroviral therapy (ART) (dolutegravir, lamivudine and tenofovir, disoproxil fumarate) and nutritional support. Locally applied drugs were avoided.
Histopathological examination revealed features of SCC with extensive necrosis along with atypical squamous cells showing dysplastic features such as basal cell hyperplasia, individual cell keratinisation, nuclear pleomorphism and altered nuclear-cytoplasmic ratio. Hence, these findings initially raised suspicion of SCC. However, the presence of abundant acute and chronic inflammatory cells, vascular congestion and vascular thrombosis warranted consideration of infectious aetiology. To confirm the diagnosis, immunohistochemistry was performed, and it showed nests of squamous cells with intact p63 and p40 and ki67 in basal lining cells. Immunohistochemical markers were not in favour of SCC which confirmed the diagnosis of cancrum oris [Figure 3].
Follow-up after one week revealed lesions of acute necrotising ulcerative gingivitis in the hard palate and gingiva of the patient. On further follow-up after two weeks, the oral lesion showed a remarkable response to treatment with a decrease in inflammation and gradual re-epithelisation, which confirmed noma infection [Figure 4]. In addition, the patient showed significant improvement in skin and ocular lesions and overall general health.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 54-year-old male presented with a 1-month history of severe oral pain, rapidly progressive oral ulceration, facial swelling, and difficulty eating and speaking, along with a 2-week history of right ocular irritation and generalized pruritic skin pustules/rashes.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the preceding 1 month, the patient developed painful, rapidly enlarging oral mucosal ulcerations accompanied by facial swelling, dysphagia, dysarthria, intermittent fevers, and right eye redness, irritation, and lower eyelid swelling. Two weeks prior to presentation, he also developed pruritic rashes and pustules over his upper arms, shoulders, trunk, and lower extremities.
subjective.past_medical_history: No previously known medical history prior to presentation.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for severe oral pain, dysphagia, dysarthria, facial swelling, intermittent fever, right eye redness/swelling, and pruritic generalized skin rash/pustules; negative for facial skin paresthesia.

objective.physical_examination: Intraoral examination revealed an extensive, rapidly progressive ulceration of the right buccal mucosa with irregular borders, central necrosis, and surrounding erythema (followed at 1 week by acute necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis involving the hard palate and gingiva); overlying external cheek skin was intact. Ocular examination showed 20/20 visual acuity bilaterally with right conjunctival injection and pustules on the right lower eyelid. Cutaneous examination revealed pruritic rashes and pustules over the shoulders, trunk, upper arms, and lower limbs. Submandibular lymph nodes were normal in size and consistency.
objective.routine_investigations: Routine blood tests and HIV serology confirmed positive HIV status. Neck ultrasonography confirmed normal lymph node size and architecture.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-cell count was 142 cells/µL. Buccal mucosal biopsy histopathology showed extensive necrosis, acute and chronic inflammatory infiltrates, vascular congestion and thrombosis, and pseudoepitheliomatous/dysplastic squamous features; immunohistochemistry demonstrated intact basal p63, p40, and Ki-67 expression, ruling out oral squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) and confirming cancrum oris (noma).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Cancrum oris (noma) and acute necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis/palatitis as the presenting manifestation of newly diagnosed AIDS (positive HIV serology, CD4+ T-cell count 142 cells/µL), differentiated from oral squamous cell carcinoma, fungal infection, tuberculosis, and leukemia by mucosal histopathology and intact basal p63/p40/Ki-67 immunohistochemical profile. Management consisted of local wound debridement, empiric broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics, nutritional support, and immediate initiation of antiretroviral therapy with dolutegravir, lamivudine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate. At 2-week follow-up, the patient demonstrated marked resolution of oral inflammation with mucosal re-epithelialization alongside significant improvement in his ocular and cutaneous lesions.
